name: Len Brune
life: Len painted the crooked arrow before he discovered how a driver's eye reads a bend. The complaints died down, but the driver who teased him became a customer for life. On Sunday, near the foot of Harbor Viaduct, Len pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: His old route passes the crooked arrow I painted in my first week. He has teased me about it for years. I've left it until after Friday so he can get in the last word.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for an unlined tan jacket and a train token tied to a zipper pull. Len has a wide brow and a narrow jaw, with a loose dark braid. Len takes off the watch before a long conversation during a conversation.
personality: Len has an appetite for a good argument about little things and works hard to keep a serious disagreement from being turned into entertainment.
agenda: To give the retired cabdriver a last chance to tease about the arrow.
family: Harley Dias is Len’s younger cousin. Len brings a spare shopping bag. Harley chooses whether they walk home or sit a while. That small arrangement gives both a reason to see each other on weeks when asking for company outright feels difficult. Asked about *A call heard twice*, Harley says, “I called the resident later about paperwork.”
connections: Nita Ellisby. The road arrow and the seat dip are two marks of the same career that these workers can preserve for a little longer.

reactions.situation: The old driver wants to change the farewell route
reactions.response: Len takes the changed route seriously and checks who needs to know the new return time.

reactions.situation: A power cut leaves two neighbors waiting on the stairs
reactions.response: Len asks which apartment is expecting someone home and makes sure that household knows about the delay.

reactions.situation: When a private quarrel becomes a public joke
reactions.response: Len says the plainest truthful thing possible and changes the subject.
